newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian clairvoyants predict UDF election win.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian clairvoyants predict UDF election win.

text.p: Bulgaria's clairvoyants agree the Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) will win a clear majority in Saturday's elections but have widely differing views on the way out of the country's economic crisis.
Clairvoyant Neika Nadeva, known as Selena, and Vili Getova from the Secret fortune-telling house, both gave predictions on Tuesday in line with more conventional opinion polls.
"I see the UDF as clear winner of the parliamentary elections on April 19 with some 61-62 percent of the votes cast," Selena told a news conference.
Both Selena and Getova said Bulgaria was a victim of black magic and the first to be affected were politicians.
Selena was more optimistic over Bulgaria's future than Getova, who predicted a difficult two years ahead though she said there was plenty of gold left over from the ancient Romans and Thracians.
"Bulgaria will get out of the deep economic crisis by 2000 and within 10 years it will become a prosperous country," Selena said.

Getova said the new government would not be able to meet the requirements of the international financial institutions and the planned currency board fixed exchange rate mechanism would run into trouble.
"Nothing will come out of the board, the conditions are difficult for us and the government will face a hurdle it will not be able to jump. Then parliament may collapse," she said.
"The richest people, and there are very rich people in Bulgaria, will take advantage of an non-working board."
Economists have also warned that powerful business interests could derail the mechanism for their own ends.
Getova promised there would eventually be a way out of the crisis, started by a "strong arm from abroad. An influential person who has no friends in the country".
She said this person would be linked to Russian President Boris Yeltsin's successor, as Bulgarian politicians would be increasingly influenced from the East, rather than the West.
She said it would not be exiled King Simeon, as the monarchy could not be restored, but Selena said the king, who lives in Madrid, would play a major role in Bulgaria's future.
"Within two years he will enter political life," she said, but added she was not able to predict in what form.

Bulgaria's best known clairvoyant, Granny Vanga, died last year aged 85. Blind from childhood, she was said to have predicted events ranging from World War Two to the collapse of communism and her own death.
Late Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev and assassinated Indian prime minister Indira Gandhi were among those reported to have consulted her over the decades.
